text.p: United Parcel Service of America Inc (UPS) and Swiss freight forwarder Danzas have established a Europe-wide freight handling cooperative deal, a UPS company statement said.
The agreement, which takes effect immediately, follows a letter of intent the two signed in June.

Danzas will be responsible for the collection, transportation and delivery of palletised shipments and freight exceeding the UPS weight and size restrictions on behalf of the U.S. company's customers, the statement added.
The Swiss forwarder will carry freight weighing more than 70 kg and palletised shipments.
While, UPS will provide Danzas with the option of using its worldwide network for express documents and package deliveries.

UPS President of Europe, Ed Reitman said: "The agreement reinforces our objective to take leadership of the worldwide express delivery markets and to focus on letters, documents and packages. Removing the transportation of heavy freight from the network improves its efficiency."
Both companies will be approaching jointly-selected new customers in order to offer tailor-made packages, said the statement.
However, the European deal will not involve any capital participation or transfer of equity,it said, with both companies continuing to operate independently.
Peter Wagner, chief executive officer of Danzas said: "Customers benefit from the complementary strengths of the two partners while allowing each company to concentrate on its core competencies."
